title: India and Denmark explore ammonia ship engines and shore power for ports
summary: India and Denmark merely discussed future ammonia engine development and port electrification, offering little immediate relief for current carbon intensity failures. While Everllence's ammonia dual-fuel engines see initial installation, these are distant solutions for a global fleet still overwhelmingly burning heavy fuel oil. Copenhagen's shore power for *cruise vessels* offers marginal emission reductions, conveniently side-stepping the urgent need for electrification among high-polluting cargo ships.
content:
India and Denmark explored cooperation on ammonia-fuelled marine engines, port electrification and alternative-fuel bunkering during an Indian ministerial visit to Copenhagen on 23 and 24 November 2026. Shantanu Thakur, India’s Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways, led a delegation of government officials and representatives from the Indian shipbuilding and ports sectors. The visit paired talks with engine developer Everllence with a review of Copenhagen’s shore power infrastructure.

India examines ammonia engines at Everllence

The delegation met Everllence’s leadership and technical teams to discuss the development and use of two-stroke marine engines capable of running on ammonia. The talks put propulsion technology and fuel infrastructure on the same agenda. For shipowners considering ammonia-fuelled vessels, the availability of bunkering infrastructure will help determine where those ships can operate on the fuel.

A separate project shows how the technology is moving into ship construction. Earlier in November, the first Everllence ammonia dual-fuel main engine for Höegh Autoliners’ Aurora-class programme was lifted into a car carrier under construction in Jiangsu, China. The engine installation is part of Höegh’s fleet programme. India’s talks with Everllence focused on examining the technology and opportunities for cooperation.

Copenhagen visit puts shore power and green bunkering in focus

At the Port of Copenhagen, Thakur met Karina Lorentzen Dehnhardt, Denmark’s Minister for Urban and Rural Affairs and Transport. The delegation visited the shore power installation and discussed how Danish ports manage electrification, plan bunkering facilities for alternative marine fuels and integrate clean energy into terminal operations.

Copenhagen inaugurated its shore power facility for cruise vessels at Oceankaj in June 2025. Onshore power supply allows compatible ships to draw electricity from land while berthed and switch off auxiliary engines used to generate onboard power. This can reduce exhaust emissions and engine noise at the berth.

Indian ports are also moving ahead with shore power. Separately from the Denmark visit, Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority awarded a ₹76.92 crore contract to Leena Powertech Engineers for a shore power project at Gateway Terminals India.

Green shipping corridor work builds on the bilateral partnership

Maritime cooperation forms part of the India–Denmark Green Strategic Partnership, launched in 2020. The two countries established the Indo-Danish Centre of Excellence on Green Shipping in 2025 to support technical cooperation on maritime decarbonisation. Its remit includes green shipbuilding, port digitalisation, seafarer training and sustainable ship recycling.

The countries also launched a pre-feasibility study on green shipping corridors in India in 2025. A 2026 workshop brought together the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, the Directorate General of Shipping and the Indian Ports Association to advance collaboration on potential corridor projects. The Copenhagen meetings added discussions with an engine developer and a port operator to that ongoing work.

FAQs

What did India and Denmark discuss during the Copenhagen visit?

The delegation examined ammonia-fuelled marine engines at Everllence and discussed shore power, port electrification and alternative-fuel bunkering at the Port of Copenhagen.

How does shore power reduce emissions at ports?

It lets compatible vessels connect to land-based electricity at berth and switch off auxiliary engines used for onboard power, reducing local exhaust emissions and noise.

What stage has India–Denmark green shipping corridor cooperation reached?

The two countries launched a pre-feasibility study in 2025 and held a workshop in 2026 to develop cooperation on potential corridor projects.
